When the meal ends, you offer the table your goodnights and leave the remaining conversation to carry on without you.

The stairs are quieter than the dining hall. In your room, the blue Council book waits beside the lamp, with the framed letter still leaning against it. Below, Garvey House continues in softened sounds—chairs moving, a door closing, someone crossing the common room—until even those fade beneath the distant storm.
